newsitem.title: USA: Enron in talks on Nepal power projects.
newsitem.headline: Enron in talks on Nepal power projects.

text.p: Enron Corp is probing possible investments in proposed hydro-electric projects in Nepal, a spokeswoman for the U.S. energy giant said on Tuesday.

"Enron has had and continues to hold very preliminary talks in Nepal on potential solar and hydro-renewable energy projects," spokeswoman Carol Hensley told Reuters. "At this point in time, it's just too early to get into any specific details regarding any of the discussions."

A team from Enron was expected to arrive in Kathmandu on Wednesday to press its offer to build a multi-billion dollar hydropower plant to export electricity to India and China, government officials there said.
"His Majesty's Government is doing the home work for starting a competitive negotiation process for the Karnali mega project," Water Resources Secretary Dwarika Nath Dhungel said.

Enron reportedly is among the bidders seeking to revive a $700 million Arun dam project. In August 1995, the World Bank pulled out of a consortium of Western donors and withdrew $175 million support for the project.

Nepali officials said the American power giant last year also offered plans to develop the proposed Karnali hydroelectric plant and export elecricity to power starved areas in neighboring India and China.
The project, estimated at $6 billion to $8 billion, also includes the installation of huge transmission lines across the Himalayas to supply electricity to China, they said.

Himalayan rivers originating in the snow covered mountains hold the potential to produce up to 83,000 megawatts of electricity, making Nepal one of the world's richest countries in terms of water resources.

But the kingdom, among the world's 10 poorest in terms of per capita gross national product, produces less than 0.50 percent of the potential and only 15 percent of its 21 million people have access to electric power.
